beats.headline: ActionRAG and ETAMem restructure how memory is retrieved
beats.summary: Relation-aware evidence retrieval and separated memory types for long-running agents.

beats.headline: Consistency and utility become the questions
beats.summary: One paper revises dependent memories when an upstream fact changes; another measures utility per task.

beats.headline: A benchmark for memory in exploration tasks
beats.summary: Graph-based benchmark and framework for long trial-and-error work such as research and software development.

open_questions: Do ActionRAG or ETAMem release code and benchmark numbers others can reproduce?
Does the dependency-aware revision method hold up on an independent long-horizon agent benchmark?
Will other memory systems report results on the new exploration-task benchmark?
Does task-conditioned utility change which memories a production agent chooses to store?

status.detail: Work has moved from retrieval design to consistency, utility measurement and benchmarks; all items are unreplicated arXiv preprints.

editorial.take_for_builders: Replay your own long-running agent traces against a plain retrieval baseline, and add a test that changes an upstream fact and checks whether dependent memories are updated; all five papers are unreplicated preprints.
editorial.tldr: agent 메모리 연구는 구조화된 검색에서 시작했습니다. ActionRAG(10월 23일)는 graph diffusion으로 관계가 일관된 근거를 찾았고, ETAMem(10월 27일)은 대화형 agent를 위해 서로 다른 메모리 유형을 분리하고 정렬했습니다.
editorial.whats_new: A Nov 4 arXiv paper adds a graph-based benchmark and framework for long-term memory in exploration tasks, after two Nov 2 papers on dependency-aware state revision and task-conditioned memory utility.
editorial.why_it_matters: The focus is shifting from how to store and retrieve memory to whether it stays consistent and useful: stale dependents, task-specific value and long trial-and-error trajectories. These are failure modes a production agent memory layer has to test for.
